subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write about the procedure involved in MRI.

mark_split.label: What MRI is and why it is safe

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.43, SAQ 46. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: What MRI is
steps.why: It uses a magnetic field rather than X-rays, which is why it can be repeated without the risk that radiation carries.
common_mistakes: Saying MRI uses X-rays. It does not.
steps.memory_tip: Magnetic Resonance Imaging: magnets, not radiation.
steps.margin_note: Full form, then why it is safe.
lines: MRI stands for Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
It is a diagnostic radiology technique.
MRI does not use ionizing radiation as in
X-rays, so it is a very safe procedure.
It produces detailed pictures of organs,
soft tissues, bones and other structures.

steps.label: The scanner
steps.why: The patient must lie inside the magnet, so the machine is built as a tube with a moving bed.
common_mistakes: Describing the scanner as an open plate.
steps.memory_tip: A giant circular magnetic tube with a sliding bed.
lines: The MRI scanner is a giant circular
magnetic tube.
The patient is placed on a movable bed
that moves into the magnetic ring.

steps.label: How the protons are used
steps.why: The body is mostly water, and the hydrogen in water gives the protons the magnet can line up.
common_mistakes: Saying the magnet detects the organs directly.
Leaving out the radio frequency field.
steps.memory_tip: Line the protons up with a magnet, then knock them with radio waves.
lines: The human body is mainly composed of
water, which contains protons.
The magnet creates a strong magnetic field.
Body protons align with the direction of
that field.
A second radio frequency field is then
turned on for a brief period.

steps.label: How the image is made
steps.why: Tissues differ in water content, so their protons release different amounts of energy and the picture shows contrast.
common_mistakes: Leaving out that the contrast comes from water content.
steps.memory_tip: Different water content gives different signal, and that is the contrast.
steps.margin_note: End with gadolinium. It is a good closing detail.
lines: The protons of different parts of the body
release different energy, which the MRI
scanner detects.
There is therefore a contrast between
images of different tissues, based on their
water content, and an image is generated.
A computer processes the information and
the images are transferred to film.

lines.text: Contrast agents like gadolinium raise accuracy

insider_note: The whole method rests on the protons in the body's water. Say so early — an answer that only describes the machine misses the physics the question is asking about.
